title: Complete intersections under flat local maps of essentially finite type field algebras
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $A$ and $B$ be commutative local $k$-algebras essentially of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra], with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A$ and $\mathfrak m_B$, and let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a flat $k$-algebra homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] which is local, meaning $\varphi(\mathfrak m_A)\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$. Put $C=B/\mathfrak m_A B$, with its induced $k$-algebra structure; it is a local $k$-algebra essentially of finite type. With complete-intersection local $k$-algebras as in [def-trf-complete-intersection-local-algebra], one has $$B\text{ is a complete-intersection local algebra over }k\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A\text{ and }C\text{ are complete-intersection local algebras over }k.$$ No completeness or separability hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 09Q7 (lemma-avramov), equivalence of (1) and (2), and Tag 09Q6 (lemma-check-lci-agrees), (1), identifying the complete-intersection notion for localizations of finite type field algebras with the local-algebra definition cited in the statement. Essentially finite type field algebras are Noetherian; quotients remain essentially finite type.

proof.text: Choose $R,S,q,v,u,F$ from [lem-sfb-compatible-regular-local-field-presentations] for $\varphi$. Put $I=\ker q$, $J=\ker v$. Surjectivity gives $A\cong R/I$ and $B\cong S/J$, while $vu=\varphi q$ gives $IS\subseteq J$. The local maps give $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_R$ and $J\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$, and surjectivity gives $q(\mathfrak m_R)=\mathfrak m_A$. Thus $\mathfrak m_AB$ is the image of $\mathfrak m_RS$ in $S/J$. Consequently $C\cong S/(J+\mathfrak m_RS)\cong F/L$, where $L=(J+\mathfrak m_RS)/\mathfrak m_RS$. The quotient-local lemma shows $C$ is local and nonzero. It is essentially of finite type over $k$: for any expression $B=W^{-1}B_0$, a quotient is $W^{-1}(B_0/H_0)$, where $H_0$ is the contraction of the quotient ideal, and $B_0/H_0$ is generated by the images of finite algebra generators. This is the defining fraction construction [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra].

source.place: Tag 09Q2 (proposition-avramov), regular presentation diagram; here compatible polynomial-local presentations suffice for the essentially finite type field-algebra special case.

proof.text: For each of the three surjections $R\twoheadrightarrow A$, $S\twoheadrightarrow B$, $F\twoheadrightarrow C$, its source is regular local and essentially of finite type over $k$. By [def-trf-complete-intersection-local-algebra], a kernel generated by a regular sequence gives the corresponding complete-intersection algebra. Conversely a complete-intersection algebra has a regular-local essentially-finite-type presentation by that definition; [lem-trf-essentially-finite-type-ci-kernel-invariance], comparing that presentation with the specified surjection, makes the specified kernel generated by a regular sequence. Hence the three complete-intersection conditions are respectively equivalent to regular-sequence generation of $I$, $J$, and $L$.

source.place: Tag 09Q6 (lemma-check-lci-agrees), proof of (1); algebra.tex Tag 00SF (lemma-lci-local), independence of the regular presentation.

proof.text: Put $T=S/IS$ and $K=J/IS$. The rings $A\cong R/I$, $T$, and $B\cong S/J$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian], since regular local rings are Noetherian. Quotient locality [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure] makes $A\to T$ local: an element of $\mathfrak m_A$ lifts to $\mathfrak m_R$, whose image in $S$ lies in $\mathfrak m_S$. It is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change], since $T\cong (R/I)\otimes_RS$. The induced quotient $T/K\cong S/J\cong B$ is flat over $A$ by hypothesis. Moreover $T/\mathfrak m_AT\cong S/\mathfrak m_RS=F$, because $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_R$, and the image of $K$ there is precisely $L$.

source.place: Tag 09Q2 (proposition-avramov), proof, the rings S/IS and their closed fibre.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-flat-quotient-nested-regular-ideals] to $R\to S$ and $I,J$. Flatness and regularity of $S/\mathfrak m_RS=F$ came from the chosen presentation; the quotient map $R/I\to S/J$ is the original flat map $A\to B$. Therefore $J$ is generated by a regular sequence exactly when both $I$ and $K=J/IS$ are generated by regular sequences in $R$ and $T$, respectively.

source.place: Tag 09PX (lemma-perfect-map-ci), (1) equivalent to (3), as applied in Tag 09Q2.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-flat-quotient-ideal-fibre-regularity] to the flat local map $A\to T$ and the ideal $K$. All its hypotheses were checked in step 3, including flatness of $T/K=B$ over $A$. Under the explicit fibre identification of that step, it gives regular-sequence generation of $K$ if and only if regular-sequence generation of $L\subset F$.

source.place: Tag 09Q2 (proposition-avramov), proof, closed-fibre comparison; Tag 0CEP and algebra.tex Tag 00MG give the ideal-level form.

proof.text: Combining steps 4 and 5 gives: $J$ is generated by a regular sequence if and only if both $I$ and $L$ are generated by regular sequences. Replace the three conditions by their equivalent complete-intersection conditions from step 2. This is exactly $B$ complete intersection over $k$ if and only if $A$ and $C$ are complete intersections over $k$.

source.place: Tag 09Q7 (lemma-avramov), conclusion for the essentially finite type field-algebra special case.
